gen-dafont-arkhip-montserrat: Montserrat glides along with big, generous curves and plenty of white space around each one. Montserrat's plain sans lines make a friendly counterweight to Arkhip, whose widely spaced letters never vary in stroke thickness.
gen-dafont-arkhip-source-serif-4:
Source Serif 4 has a dignified, gently swelling stroke.

Arkhip sits above it with spaced-out letters and no hairlines anywhere, so the page moves between one flat line and a softly breathing one.
gen-dafont-arkhip-work-sans: Modern through and through, Arkhip spreads its letters wide and keeps every stroke uniform. And Work Sans, a plain sans with a high mean line, handles the quieter job of keeping text lines tidy and its c tips well apart.
gen-dafont-azonix-fs-alpino:
Flat, single-weight linework gives Azonix its commanding look.

Alpino's tall, cozy body makes ascenders look short, and its tight spacing and open curve endings make a long passage feel casual and compact.
gen-dafont-azonix-fs-epilogue:
Azonix has wide-mouthed capitals that stay crisp even when shrunk down.

Epilogue brings curvy, wire-like monoline letters with stubby ascenders, so its size can stay modest while the sans still reads comfortably.
gen-dafont-azonix-fs-familjen-grotesk:
Commanding and wide, Azonix takes the lead.

Familjen Grotesk, a lively sans with tall lowercase and bowls left open on one side, can sit a notch smaller beneath it without losing any presence.
gen-dafont-azonix-fs-hind:
Azonix leads with authority, its wide letters drawn in one flat line.

Hind follows as a plain sans with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals, and the strokes stay taut like a drawn string, so the two keep the page orderly without competing.
gen-dafont-azonix-fs-hoover:
Wide, flat and stern.

Hoover, a refined classic serif with a generous e and compressed ascenders, makes long paragraphs feel sturdy and settled, a firm contrast to Azonix's unchanging pen.
gen-dafont-azonix-fs-ranade:
A pen that never shifts pressure defines Azonix.

It excels at commanding, wide-mouthed headlines, while Ranade does the gentler work of spreading its organic, slightly varied sans strokes across a roomy line.
gen-dafont-azonix-fs-rowan:
Rowan is a literary, friendly text serif whose curves open generously and whose thin strokes carry real weight beside the thick ones.

After Azonix's flat headline, it reads warmly.
